findings.message: The proxy now calls the app's getDb() to set up its own bundle. getDb() decides whether to wire things by checking a cache kept on globalThis (`cache.amaxDb`), and on k3s and the standalone image the proxy and the app share that globalThis. Every request passes through the proxy first, so the proxy's getDb() fills the shared cache and wires only the proxy bundle's copies of configureRuntime, setGrants, setPrivacySources, installAuthorizer, configureAi and the rate limits. When the app bundle later calls getDb(), the cache is already set, so it returns the Db without wiring the app bundle's own copies of those modules. An earlier lesson in this repo found that Next compiles the proxy and the app as separate bundles that don't share module state. So the fix moves the Vercel/Cloudflare problem onto k3s. Importing lib/server also pulls every module manifest, its UI screens, the AI providers and node:fs into the proxy bundle. Fix: key the 'already wired' flag per bundle (a module-scoped flag, separate from the shared Db cache), or give the proxy a small wiring entry that sets up only the rate limits and the recorder. Then test both orders: proxy first and app first.
findings.scenario: k3s pod starts and the first request is a page load. proxy.ts runs getDb(), which sets globalThis.amaxDb and wires the proxy bundle. The page's server code then calls getDb() in the app bundle, finds the cache set and skips wiring. The app bundle's runtime, authorizer, privacy sources and AI stay unconfigured, so services fail, or run without the configured authorizer, until the process restarts.

findings.message: The previous round's major (page 429s are not recorded when the proxy runs apart from the app) is backed only by a test that greps proxy.ts for the string 'getDb();' and checks it comes before 'takeRate('. The other new test calls wireRateLimits directly in the test process. Neither one drives the proxy. Neither would fail if getDb() skipped the rate wiring (for example, because the cache was already set, or because DATABASE_URL gating returns early), and neither would fail if the proxy's sink never reached api.rate_limited. Fix: add a table-driven test that loads the proxy entry in its own module graph (vi.resetModules or a separate import, so it doesn't share the app's state), sends page requests past the limit for at least three cases (proxy-only process, proxy first then app, app first then proxy), and checks that a row lands in api.rate_limited.
findings.scenario: Change getDb() so it skips wireRateLimits when cache.amaxDb is already set. Both new tests still pass, yet page 429s in a separate proxy process are never recorded and the 'Pages' row reads 0.

findings.message: [design] Rows found only by name are now left out of the erase and the access package. That fixes the over-reach. But the request still moves to approved and completed, and the screen says 'Erased' or 'Package ready', while those rows stay unresolved. Nothing tracks them after completion, and no MCP or chat write tool lets a person erase or export a specific row once they've checked it. The Item doc says 'check and change in chat', but no such tool exists. Presales activity, task and risk still have no subject id column, so for those tables a subject's own rows are never erased or exported. Those requests are recorded as done when they are only partly done. Fix: keep a request with review rows in a 'needs review' state, not completed. Add a chat write tool that confirms or rejects named rows for the request, so they are then erased or exported. Or add the id columns the earlier finding asked for.
findings.scenario: An erasure for Rowan, whose presales tasks record only owner_name 'Rowan Test' → complete_privacy_request → status completed ('Erased …; 1 record recorded by name only, to check by hand') → the task row still holds the name, and no tool can erase it.

findings.message: [design] The test 'a period stored below the floor still runs at the floor' calls effective() with a hand-built rule. It never runs previewPurge or purgeDue, whose period comes from periodOf/widest. So it doesn't show that a P1D override stored before this change (an Admin already shortened api.inbound) is purged at P90D. Fix: drive previewPurge over pt.note rows aged 30 and 100 days with the P1D override stored, and expect only the 100-day row to be due.

[design] webhookEvents dedupes by event name with a Map, so when two manifests emit the same event the last declaration wins. A looser 'plain' declaration can then replace a classified one. Fix: merge the declarations, keeping the stricter class for each field, or reject duplicate emitters.

The rate-limit paragraph still says counts are 'shared by the proxy's and the app's bundles'. That is false on Vercel and Cloudflare, where the proxy now wires its own limiter. The new outgoing-webhooks sentence is also garbled ('payload fields of a each module declares…').
